body.statement: For every \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), the observed law \(P_X\) first determines only the unstructured \(q^K\)-label set \(\mathscr L(P_X)\) through generic three-view uniqueness; the component-equality pattern \(\mathcal E(P_X)\) then uniquely aligns those labels with \(K\) \(q\)-state coordinates through \(\varphi_{\mathrm{coord}}\), modulo \(\mathfrak G\), and latent conditional independences determine \([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\). Consequently \(P_X\) uniquely determines \(\mathcal R(P_X)=[\Gamma,\pi,p,[\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}]_{\sim}\); equivalently, every realization in the fully enumerated domain \(\mathcal C_K(P_X)\) belongs to the same \(\sim\)-equivalence class.
body.justification: The theorem separates generic mixture-label recovery from the new coordinate-alignment argument that identifies the measurement graph and latent MEC.
body.gap: Lee and Gu (2026, Theorem 2) cover binary latents; Allman et al. (2009) identify an arbitrary latent-class label set but do not recover its \(K\)-coordinate product structure, measurement adjacency, or latent MEC.
body.consumer: It certifies that a recovered polytomous skill graph and latent MEC are not artifacts of another same-dimension BLCM realization.
body.proof_tex:
Set \(r=q^K\), and regard the joint observed law on the three disjoint views as a three-way tensor. For \(z\in\mathcal Q^{|S_3|}\), let \(T_z\) be its \(r\times r\) slice at \(X_{S_3}=z\), and let \(m_3(z\mid h)=P(X_{S_3}=z\mid H=h)\). Conditional independence of observed variables given \(H\) gives
\[
 T_z=M_1\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\pi_hm_3(z\mid h):h\in\mathcal Q^K\bigr)M_2^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} makes \(M_1,M_2\) invertible, and positive support makes \(\operatorname{diag}(\pi)\) invertible. Therefore \(T_{12}=\sum_zT_z\) is invertible and
\[
 C_z:=T_zT_{12}^{-1}
 =M_1\operatorname{diag}\bigl(m_3(z\mid h):h\in\mathcal Q^K\bigr)M_1^{-1}.
\]

The third-view component columns are pairwise distinct. Indeed, if \(h\ne h'\), choose \(k\) with \(h_k\ne h'_k\). Third-view coverage provides \(j\in S_3\) with \(k\in A_j\); the two parent configurations at \(j\) differ, so measurement nondegeneracy makes the conditional marginal columns for \(X_j\), and hence the joint columns \(m_3(\cdot\mid h)\) and \(m_3(\cdot\mid h')\), distinct.

There is consequently a real vector \(t=(t_z)_z\) for which all numbers
\[
 \lambda_h=\sum_z t_zm_3(z\mid h)
\]
are distinct: the excluded choices are the finite union of proper hyperplanes \(t\cdot(m_3(\cdot\mid h)-m_3(\cdot\mid h'))=0\). The observable matrix \(C(t)=\sum_zt_zC_z\) has simple spectrum and eigenvectors equal to the columns of \(M_1\), up to one common permutation and nonzero column scalings. Normalizing each eigenvector to have entries summing to one removes the scalings because each true column is a probability vector. Then
\[
 W=M_1^{-1}T_{12}=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)M_2^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \pi_h=\sum_{x_2}W(h,x_2),
 \qquad
 M_2^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)^{-1}W,
\]
where division is valid by positive support. Finally \(M_1^{-1}C_zM_1\) recovers every \(m_3(z\mid h)\). Marginalizing the recovered joint-view columns recovers the conditional column of every individual observed variable. Thus \(P_X\) determines the component labels, weights, and all measurement columns up to one arbitrary permutation of the \(r\) labels.

Theorem~\textnormal{thm:coordinate-alignment} now transforms those anonymous labels into the unique \(K\)-coordinate product modulo \(\mathfrak G\), recovers \(\Gamma,\pi,p\), and recovers \([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\) from faithfulness. This proves that \(P_X\) determines \(\mathcal R(P_X)\).

It remains to justify the comparison-domain assertion. Any element of \(\mathcal C_K(P_X)\) supplies another \(r\)-term product decomposition of the same three-view tensor with all \(r\) weights positive. Since \(T_{12}\) has rank \(r\), both alternative first- and second-view factor matrices must have rank \(r\). Applying that alternative decomposition to the observable simple-spectrum matrix \(C(t)\) shows that its first-view columns are the same eigenvectors, up to the same permutation and probability normalization. The displayed formulas then force the same weights, second-view columns, and third-view columns. Its measurement nondegeneracy and subset condition imply, by the lattice proof of Theorem~\textnormal{thm:coordinate-alignment}, the same coordinate factors and \(\Gamma\) modulo \(\mathfrak G\). Its faithfulness gives the same latent Markov equivalence class. Hence every comparison-domain realization lies in the same \(\sim\)-class, as claimed.
